1627: G.Glossary
1628: 
1629: G.1Ability
1630: 
1631: A persistent effect of a faction as listed at the top of its faction board and in its Faction Rules and Abilities section, or a persistent effect of a hireling as listed on its hireling card (H.2.2).
1632: 
1633: G.2Adjacent
1634: 
1635: A clearing is adjacent to all other clearings linked to it by a path. A forest is adjacent to all clearings that touch it without crossing a path, and it is adjacent to all forests that are separated by only one path, except on the lake (M.3.4).
1636: 
1637: G.3Building
1638: 
1639: A square cardboard piece owned by its faction or hireling.
1640: 
1641: G.4Cannot
1642: 
1643: See 1.1.2. The term cannot is absolute. It cannot be overridden unless explicitly instructed.
1644: 
1645: G.5Discard
1646: 
1647: Place the prompted card in the shared discard pile. If it is a dominance card, place it near the map instead (3.3.3).
1648: 
1649: G.6Draw
1650: 
1651: Take a card into your hand. If drawing from a deck or pile, take the top card unless otherwise specified. If no source is specified, take it from the shared deck (2.1).
1652: 
1653: G.7Effect
1654: 
1655: Anything that changes the game, including persistent effects, faction abilities, and actions.
1656: 
1657: G.8Enemy
1658: 
1659: Any other player that you are not in a coalition with (9.2.8), or a hireling that is in the supply or held by an enemy player.
1660: 
1661: G.9Enemy Piece
1662: 
1663: A faction piece of an enemy player or a hireling piece of an enemy hireling, except while you're treating the piece as your own for rule *(Riverfolk mercenaries, controlled hirelings, etc.)*. *(Items cannot be enemy pieces.)*
1664: 
1665: G.10Faction Piece
1666: 
1667: All the warriors, pawns, buildings, and tokens listed on the back of a faction board. *(Items are not faction pieces.)* See 1.5.1.
1668: 
1669: G.11Forest
1670: 
1671: An area on the map enclosed by paths and clearings.
1672: 
1673: G.12Force
1674: 
1675: See 1.5.5.
1676: 
1677: G.13Item
1678: 
1679: A square cardboard piece showing an item (, , , etc.) that is not owned by any faction.
1680: 
1681: G.14Map
1682: 
1683: See 2.2.
1684: 
1685: G.15Map Edge
1686: 
1687: The single closed loop of clearings and paths that define the map boundary, including closed paths on the mountain map.
1688: 
1689: G.16Matching
1690: 
1691: Of the same suit.
1692: 
1693: G.17Path
1694: 
1695: A white link between two clearings.
1696: 
1697: G.18Pawn
1698: 
1699: A wooden figure owned by its faction or hireling.
1700: 
1701: G.19Piece
1702: 
1703: Any component—building, token, warrior, pawn, item, marker, and so on.
1704: 
1705: G.20Place
1706: 
1707: Take the prompted piece from the prompted source and put it in the prompted destination. Usually, no source is specified—in this case, take it from its supply, or take the leftmost prompted piece if it is on a track. Put is shorthand for Place.
1708: 
1709: G.21Play Area
1710: 
1711: The area around your faction board. Cards in it can only be spent, discarded, or used for other purposes if explicitly instructed.
1712: 
1713: G.22Random
1714: 
1715: When referring to a card, choose one at random without looking at them at all.
1716: 
1717: G.23Replace
1718: 
1719: Remove the prompted piece and place the other prompted piece in the location from which the first was removed. To do so, you must be able to complete both steps. *(For example, enemies of the Marquise cannot replace a Marquise warrior at the keep.)*
1720: 
1721: G.24Remove
1722: 
1723: Take the prompted piece from the prompted source and return it to the prompted destination. Usually, no destination is specified—in this case, return it to its owner's supply, return it to the rightmost empty space of its track it has one, or remove it permanently otherwise. *(Items are removed permanently.)*
1724:

1726: 
1727: Place the prompted card face up in your play area. Usually, no source is specified—in this case, take it from your hand.

1738: 
1739: A player rules a clearing if they have more total warriors and buildings in it than each other player. *(Tokens and pawns do not contribute to rule.)* If there is a tie between players in a clearing, no one rules it.
